303A.4 / CHAPTER 4 OF 11

Adding up or down

Is the reason to add stronger than the price change?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Choose the container02Opportunity vs portfolio risk03Scout, then earn promotion04Adding up or down05Harvest & residual exposure06Reset the mission07Break the attachment08Attention & holding time09Match the evidence to the market10Portfolio limits & concentration11Measure the net result

01Definition

Averaging changes your entry cost and total exposure. Its rationale depends on evidence and limits, not direction alone.

02Why it matters

A cheaper price can accompany a weaker thesis; a higher price can accompany better information.

03What to check

  • What improved independently of price
  • Whether the original invalidation still holds
  • New total exposure, exit depth, and risk budget

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

The add survives a fresh review of evidence and cost.

Dangerous

A falling price becomes the entire reason to buy more.

05Beginner mistake

Improving the average while worsening portfolio risk.

06Takeaway

Cheaper is not evidence.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    Price falls below the first entry.

  2. 02

    The trader wants to add, but buyers and liquidity are weakening.

  3. 03

    A lower average does not repair the deteriorating case.

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

Buying $100 at 1.00 and $100 at 0.50 acquires 300 units for $200, averaging about 0.667 before costs. The lower average does not improve the token’s permissions or restore disappeared demand.

How to investigate it

For any add, calculate new quantity, cost basis, total cash committed, current exposure, and exit quotes. Explain what improved independently of price and whether the original invalidation still holds. Apply the same evidence requirement to adds after rises and after falls.

Check your reasoning — answered

Your thesis is invalidated at 0.50, but averaging lowers break-even. Did the lower average repair the thesis? No. It changes accounting, not the supporting evidence.

Try it on a token

See it in Meme Fast → Swing

Review observed structure and reported liquidity, then check sampled flow in Inspect. These do not determine your add size or execution price.

Go deeper

Neither averaging up nor averaging down is automatically justified. Review location, thesis, current hygiene, invalidation, and fresh risk together. A technically attractive area can still fail; a stronger thesis can still be too expensive or too illiquid for the intended order.
